items.headline: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
items.blurb: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
items.text: France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions. Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless. The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked. Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people". He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond

items.headline: Pope meets with clergy abuse survivors in Argentina
items.blurb: During private meetings with survivors, Pope Leo XIV pledged to reinforce safeguards and listen to victims.
items.text: Pope Leo XIV has met with five survivors of clerical sexual abuse on the second day of his historic visit to Argentina. The private meetings in Buenos Aires on Monday were the first of several talks the pope is planning to hold with abuse survivors during his 12-day tour of Latin America, according to the Vatican. “The Pope spoke individually with each of them, listened to their words and to the painful stories of their experiences, as well as to their proposals for strengthening paths towards healing within the Church,” the Vatican said in a statement. The closed-door meetings followed a historic open-air mass that drew an estimated 2.5 million people to Avenida del Libertador, a major boulevard in the capital, at the Monumento de los Espanoles. It was the country’s first papal liturgy in nearly 40 years. The meetings with survivors respond to the pope’s desire to “express his closeness to those who have suffered”, build paths to healing and ensure the church is a safe and “spiritually healthy” place, the Holy See Press Office said in October. items.headline: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
items.blurb: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
items.text: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said. The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways. items.headline: Trump says Nvidia boss told him he had no idea woman he had affair with was Chinese spy
items.blurb: The US president said the FBI is now investigating the affair. He said he spoke with Jensen Huang and asked him about the affair.
items.text: Donald Trump has said the boss of Nvidia, whose affair with an alleged Chinese spy is being investigated, told him that he had "no idea she was a spy". The US President said he spoke with CEO Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign. "I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. Trump said the FBI was also investigating the affair. China has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Nvidia, who commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. items.headline: Hungarian police reportedly detain brother of ex-PM Viktor Orban
items.blurb: Aron Orban reportedly detained as Hungarian authorities raid properties linked to his business associates.
items.text: Former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban has accused the country’s new government of “political persecution” after the reported arrest of his younger brother. Hungarian police arrested Aron Orban on Monday on suspicion of people smuggling, among other offences, according to a press report shared by Prime Minister Peter Magyar. Viktor Orban’s staunch opposition to immigration defined his 16 years in power that ended in defeat at elections in April. News of the arrest was first reported by Kontroll, a news site owned by Magyar’s brother, Marton. Police carried out raids involving Aron Orban’s business associates but did not confirm whether he was among those detained, local media reported. Viktor Orban accused the government of arresting his brother as a way to “divert attention” from other issues. “I am the real target. My younger brother is simply being used to get to me,” he wrote on X. Like other members of the Orban family, Aron built several successful businesses during his brother’s rule. See My World , a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November. The festival is part of See My World’s year-round programme showcasing pan-African arts, culture and events. items.headline: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.blurb: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.
items.text: Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair. Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China. However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort". items.headline: Saudi Arabia reports new attack on key East-West pipeline
items.blurb: The oil pipeline runs through the desert to the coast and is essential for bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.
items.text: Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline has suffered another attack, according to state media. An official at the Saudi Ministry of Energy said that the pipeline was targeted in the Medina region in the west of the country on Monday, causing a “limited fire” that was extinguished, the Saudi Press Agency reported. “No injuries or fatalities were reported, and pipeline operations were unaffected,” it said. The report did not identify the party behind the attack, but fighting continues to intensify between Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government coalition that it backs, and the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen. The pipeline is essential for bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, which remains tightly constricted by the US-Israel war on Iran. It has come under attack several times as the war on Iran fuels a global energy crisis . The Houthis have also repeatedly targeted Saudi oil infrastructure, including refineries and storage facilities, with drones and missiles. items.headline: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
items.blurb: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
items.text: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history. The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes. Prosecutors said Paul Mackenzie and his Good News International church ran ​a Christian doomsday sect whose members were ordered to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended. His accomplices threatened and beat victims to ensure they followed his orders. The emaciated bodies were found scattered in shallow graves and dumped in latrines. Some had been buried alive. items.headline: Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 17 people
items.blurb: Eyewitnesses say the explosion shook the ground, with one believing an earthquake had hit near the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga.
items.text: At least 17 people have died and 12 others have been injured in an explosion at an iron and steel factory near the port city of Izmir in western Turkey. All those killed and injured were workers at the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga, one of the country's leading steel producers, authorities said. Footage from the scene showed a large fire inside the facility and a towering column of smoke rising into the air. The local governor said the blast happened around midday after a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed, causing materials to fall into a furnace below. Workplace accidents remain a chronic problem in Turkey, the Turkish Health and Safety Labor Watch, an independent civil society organisation, said. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan originally said the death toll was 16, but the Health Minister, Kemal Memişoğlu, later announced that one of those who had been critically injured had later died, taking the toll to 17. items.blurb: Odisha cabinet approves proposal for ₹4,708-crore pumped storage project
items.text: Bhubaneswar, The Odisha cabinet on Monday approved 13 proposals, including a ₹ 4,708-crore 600 MW pumped storage project, free Wi-Fi for college students and unlimited attempts for candidates appearing in the state civil services examination till the prescribed upper age limit. The proposals were approved at a cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi here. "The cabinet has approved… the 600 MW Upper Indravati Pumped Storage Project at Ranibahal, Kalahandi district. The state will spend a total of ₹ 4,708.64 crore, including ₹ 3,371.88 crore for construction of the project," Chief Secretary Anu Garg told reporters. Describing it as the first project of its kind in the state, Garg said it is targeted to be commissioned by the 2030–31 financial year. Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd has been selected as the project developer. The 600 MW facility will generate approximately 1,040 million units of annual peak electricity, officials said. We saw ‘vote chori’ in West Bengal, Bihar, Haryana, Maharashtra etc. In entire India 13 crore voters were dropped from the voter list. Ladakh is a small region and fraud is easy,” said Ladakh Buddhist Association (LBA) chairman Tsering Dorjey Lakrook. Terming the upcoming panchayat and municipal elections as “conspiracy against people of Ladakh”, Mr. Lakrook, who is also co-chairman of the Leh Apex Body (LAB), said, “I warn people of Ladakh that these elections are a conspiracy. People of Ladakh should stay awake. We demand postponement of these elections. Let the authorities first frame the constituencies and hold the election in April-May next year,” said Mr. Lakrook. items.headline: India-EU review FTA progress ahead of PM Modi's Brussels visit, push investment and trade ties
items.blurb: India and the EU reviewed engagements aimed at boosting trade and investment cooperation, including the timely signing, implementation of the India-EU FTA.
items.text: India and the European Union (EU) on Monday reviewed efforts aimed at the timely signing and implementation of a free trade agreement and to conclude an investment protection agreement and an agreement on geographical indications. These matters figured at an India-EU strategic partnership review meeting held in New Delhi, weeks ahead of an expected visit by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Brussels in mid-December for the signing of the FTA. The two sides concluded negotiations for the trade deal in January. India and the EU reviewed engagements aimed at boosting trade and investment cooperation, including the “timely signing and implementation of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement”, and to conclude the investment protection agreement and the agreement on geographical indications, both sides said in a joint statement. The discussions also covered strengthening supply chains and economic security, including strategic engagements in the Trade and Technology Council (TTC) and Blue Valleys initiative. items.headline: Six of family killed in fire at home above grocery store in Maharashtra
items.blurb: A boy, who was brought downstairs to safety by his parents before they went back in an effort to rescue the others, was the sole survivor
items.text: Six members of a family — two teenage girls, their parents, and their grandparents — were killed after a fire broke out at their house above a grocery store in Maharashtra’s Dharashiv district in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026). A boy, who was brought downstairs to safety by the parents before they went back in an effort to rescue the others, was the sole survivor. The fire broke out around 2.30 a.m. in Yedshi village at the residence of Govind Uttam Karande (47), whose family lived on the upper floor of a building housing their grocery store, said Prakash Vhatkar, an official from the Dharashiv Revenue Office. The deceased have been identified as Uttam Trimbak Karande (75), his wife Chandrakala Uttam Karande (70), their son Govind Uttam Karande (47), his wife Jyoti Govind Karande (42), and the couple’s daughters Gayatri (16) and Siddhi (15). items.headline: Bihar govt bans firecrackers near ghats, private boat operations during Chhath Puja
items.blurb: The Bihar Disaster Management Department has directed all districts to enforce strict safety measures during Chhath Puja from November 13 to 16.
items.text: The Bihar Disaster Management Department has directed all districts to enforce strict safety measures during Chhath Puja (November 13–16), including a ban on firecrackers near ghats and private boat operations, officials said. According to a statement issued by the department on Monday, district magistrates have been asked to identify and barricade dangerous ghats, and deploy adequate security personnel and volunteers. It has also directed that trained divers, swimmers, motorboats and life-saving equipment be stationed at river ghats. Medical teams, ambulances and Quick Medical Response Teams (QMRTs) must remain on standby, the statement said. The directives also call for adequate lighting at ghats and approach roads, round-the-clock functioning of district control rooms and continuous public announcements through loudspeakers. All electrical installations must be inspected in advance to prevent electrocution, it said. To prevent panic and stampedes, district magistrates have been asked to prepare disaster management and communication plans, hold coordination meetings with Chhath committees and ensure strict monitoring throughout the festival. items.text: SAO PAULO, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Shareholders and creditors of Brazilian petrochemical company Braskem are aiming to conclude out-of-court restructuring talks by Wednesday, two people close to the negotiations over the multibillion-dollar deal told Reuters on Monday. Braskem faces a November 22 court deadline to present an approved restructuring plan for close to $11 billion in debt. If it misses that deadline, it will face a formal judicial recovery, a type of court-supervised bankruptcy protection that all parties want to avoid. An attempt to reach an agreement with bondholders in New York failed last week after shareholders and bondholders disagreed on the scale of the deal, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity because discussions are private. The planned recapitalization of the company controlled by private equity firm IG4 and oil producer Petrobras includes a capital injection by shareholders and a debt-to-equity conversion by creditors, they said. items.headline: JPMorgan Weighs Big Discount to Lure Lenders for Software Debt
items.blurb: Banks led by JPMorgan Chase & Co. could offer one of the year’s biggest discounts to sell some of the $5 billion in debt for software firm Qualtrics International Inc. that the underwriters were stuck holding a few months ago.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- Banks led by JPMorgan Chase & Co. could offer one of the year’s biggest discounts to sell some of the $5 billion in debt for software firm Qualtrics International Inc. that the underwriters were stuck holding a few months ago. Bankers have scheduled meetings with investors this week to discuss the sale of nearly $2 billion of debt in the high-yield bond market, according to people with knowledge of the matter. Initial indications are that the debt could be marketed at a coupon of at least 8% and a discounted rate of about 85 cents on the dollar, said the people, requesting anonymity as the talks are private. If a deal was struck at that price, it would represent one of the biggest new-issue discounts for a debt sale in the US high-yield market this year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. A number of software companies have had to pay high borrowing costs and boost protections to lock in lenders in recent months, as concerns about AI-disruption to their businesses have intensified. items.text: Europe is set to benefit from recent market turmoil in the US as investors seek a safe haven, according to European Investment Bank President Nadia Calvino. “Turbulence in the US is making capital flow to Europe,” she told Bloomberg TV in an interview on Monday. “I expect that to continue.” Calvino said she doesn’t see any negative impact on investment in Europe at the moment, adding that there had been very strong demand for EIB bond issuance and that she expects more of the same in January. “Right now we’re confronted with turbulence and instability in the financial markets, so it’s of the utmost importance that we preserve Europe as a safe haven in this context,” she said. Calvino, who heads the Luxembourg-based institution that is effectively the lending arm of the European Union, was speaking as euro-area finance ministers meet in Brussels for the first time since nominations closed for candidates to replace European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde. The Noida-based company also continues to face profitability challenges in its offline business, despite the expansion of its Vidyapeeth centres. During its Q2 FY27 earnings call, management confirmed that its total employee count, which stood at around 19,100, and faculty strength of approximately 7,100 declined sequentially in the quarter. The firm attributed the reduction partly to efficiencies from AI across content creation, quality checks, test paper preparation and evaluation. Management said AI now writes around 90% of the company's code. The shift towards automation has also helped contain employee expenses, which declined 2.3% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, excluding ESOP costs. For the first half of FY27, employee expenses were down 2.4% compared to the same period last year. However, PhysicsWallah continues to invest in technology which stood at Rs 104 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 70 crore in the corresponding period last year. items.headline: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
items.blurb: "Do not ask again" prompt leads to passwords, API keys, and more being shared.
items.text: Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That’s the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets , including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories. The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the “Yes, and don’t ask again” option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local “.claude/settings.local.json” file on the user’s computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it. This isn’t really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user’s local machine (assuming that machine doesn’t become compromised itself, of course). For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance. Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments. items.text: As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape. Driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ. It’s accepted wisdom in Big Tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures.” It’s a culture war, in other words. But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. AI’s power crunch has become so acute that Anthropic, a company that has generally avoided buying physical infrastructure, is spending $3.4 billion on natural gas turbines. The AI company, which is planning to go public this year, is buying Caterpillar generators that equipment supplier OnePWR had originally ordered, according to a Financial Times report . The generators are capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts of electricity. Historically, Anthropic has preferred to rent rather than buy. The company disclosed in its S-1 filing in May that it is paying SpaceX subsidiary xAI $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 to use xAI’s computing power. “We expect to enter into additional similar services contracts,” Anthropic stated in the filing, meaning more deals to rent computing power.
